title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. translated_title: 更努力思考并不能带来更好的选择：推理努力提升了LLM购物代理的置信度，而非正确性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被部署为自主购物代理，它们处理多模态商品信息（包括视觉和文本数据）并代表消费者推荐购买。人们自然会认为，思考能力更强的模型会做出更高质量的购买决策。为了验证这一观点，我们针对此类代理提出了两个问题：要求模型更努力地思考，是否会让它选出更好的产品？它所报告的置信度，能否告诉我们它出错的概率？我们在基于WebShop、亚马逊SQID和Wayfair的WANDS平台构建的三个产品选择基准上，对十个前沿模型进行了测试，以检验思考能力更强的LLM是否真的能做出更高质量的产品购买决策。在全部三个基准上，我们发现增加思考努力并不能在统计上显著提升决策质量。而同样的思考努力变化却会提高模型所声称的置信度（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 在三个购物基准测试中，增加LLM购物代理的推理努力并不能显著提升其选购产品的正确性，却会显著提高其报告的置信度——也就是说，模型“想得更多”只是变得更自信，而不是变得更正确。
en_tdlr: Across three shopping benchmarks, increasing reasoning effort makes LLM shopping agents more confident but not more correct in their product choices.
